finding: Bickel et al. 2024 detection positions carry per-source-image georeferencing errors of ~1-3.5 km relative to the ISIS camera model (spiceinit, reconstructed kernels).

evidence.method: shift maximizing high-pass brightness anomaly under the image's own detections; at zero shift the anomaly is ~0 in all four images, at the best shift 4-9 sigma
evidence.visual: a5_shift_demo.png: in CN0254138067M the catalogued polygons sit 1.5-2 km north of unmistakable hollow clusters; shifted polygons land on them

not_a_projection_problem: GeoPackage CRS, longitude convention and geometry/attribute agreement verified; the shift differs in direction per image so it is not a convention error
recompute_not_possible: 'Image x/y coord (pix)' columns are normalized 0-1 but are NOT full-frame coordinates (all 8 axis conventions give >14 km residuals via campt); presumably tile-relative (thumbnail tags M2, M3...), tile layout not released
implications: project analyses at >=8 ppd (14 km cells) unaffected
per-detection work at <3 km (QGIS overlays on NAC frames, halo/pit matching) must expect 1-3.5 km displacement
A5 remains a valid Priority A site: hollow fields are present in three source images
coarse-resolution (>100 m/px, low-incidence) detections additionally look like bright ejecta at 35 m/px and should be treated as 'bright material'
options: per-image shift correction by texture correlation where hollows are bright (risk: chases bright craters where n is small)
hand-tie polygons per site in QGIS
contact the catalogue authors for tile geometry or full-frame pixel coordinates -> exact recomputation via campt
